tier_reason: Upgraded from C: HPTT's peer-reviewed ARRAY 2017 paper (Springer, Su, Bientinesi; arXiv 1704.04374, linked from the README) reports, per a search-result quote of its abstract, up to 27.4x over Eigen's tensor transposition (Eigen is a listed baseline) and up to 3.1x faster CTF contractions after integrating HPTT. The paper is blocked here and the repo has no Eigen harness (benchmark/benchmark.cpp compares only with a naive reference), so not A. The README's own numpy figure is first-party.

corrections.baseline: Eigen tensor transposition (Eigen::Tensor shuffle), per the ARRAY 2017 paper; the README additionally compares with numpy.transpose (np.transpose(A, perm).copy(order=order) in pythonAPI/benchmark/benchmark.py)
corrections.claimed_speedup: ARRAY 2017 paper abstract, as quoted by a search result (paper not opened): up to 27.4x faster than Eigen's tensor transposition, bandwidth comparable to SAXPY, and up to 3.1x faster tensor contractions when HPTT is integrated into CTF. README figure misc/hptt_vs_numpy.png (bar chart, values read by eye): 57 test cases, speedup over numpy.transpose from about 5.1x (case 46) to about 19.7x (case 42), most between 7x and 13x, HPTT on 24 threads of 2x Xeon E5-2680 v3.
corrections.workload: Out-of-place tensor transposition. Paper: HPTT vs Eigen tensor shuffle over the TTC benchmark permutations (details not seen). README figure: 57 permutation/size cases, HPTT tensorTransposeAndUpdate with 24 threads vs numpy.transpose(...).copy(); the current pythonAPI/benchmark/benchmark.py allocates A and B as np.float64 regardless of its --floatType option, times with time.time() taking the minimum of 5 runs, and 'trashes' cache by updating a 2500x2500 float array between runs.
corrections.caveats: The Eigen numbers (up to 27.4x) come from the peer-reviewed ARRAY 2017 paper, which could not be opened (arXiv, sigplan.org and ACM blocked); only the abstract was seen via search results, so the CPU, compiler, thread counts and per-case figures behind 27.4x are unverified, and the repo has no Eigen harness. The README's numpy comparison is HPTT on 24 threads against a numpy copy whose thread count is not stated (numpy's copy is normally single-threaded), so the 5-20x range mostly shows multi-threaded bandwidth use; HPTT also applies alpha/beta while the numpy side only copies; figure values are read by eye. The repo's C++ benchmark (benchmark/benchmark.cpp) compares only against an in-repo naive OpenMP reference transposition and optionally the original TTC. benchmark/bw.png (paper Fig. 6) shows HPTT bandwidth with and without autotuning against the system SAXPY and STREAM lines on Ivy Bridge, KNL, IBM Power7, AMD and ARM machines, not against a named library. Repository unmaintained since 2022. A transposition library is BLAS-adjacent rather than a BLAS/LAPACK routine, so the category is a loose fit.

notes: README page (original benchmark_url) compares only with numpy, and its figure values match the record (5.1x to 19.7x); the corrected benchmark_url (arXiv paper, Eigen comparison) could not be opened. The record's 'float32' was wrong for the current script (arrays are float64). Metadata confirmed: BSD-3-Clause, 205 stars, 52 forks, last commit 2022-02-15 'removed lGPLv3 from remaining files' (abandoned). A retier to A would need the paper's Eigen harness and setup.
